name: DAYS
description: DAYS returns the number of days between two dates by subtracting the start date from the end date; note that the argument order is (end_date, start_date).
tldr: Counts the days from start_date to end_date.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: The later date. This is the FIRST argument, the opposite of the intuitive order.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: The earlier date. This is the SECOND argument.

basicExample.description: Days between the 1st and 15th of January
basicExample.explanation: end_date (Jan 15) minus start_date (Jan 1) is 14 days. Note that end_date comes first.

advancedExamples.title: Spanning two months including a leap day
advancedExamples.scenario: From Jan 1 to Mar 1 in a leap year
advancedExamples.description: Counts each day across the boundary
advancedExamples.explanation: January (31 days) plus February 2024 (29 days, leap year) equals 60 days.

advancedExamples.title: Reversed dates give a negative result
advancedExamples.description: Order matters: end first, start second
advancedExamples.explanation: Because the earlier date is first, the result is negative (Jan 1 minus Jan 15 = -14).

howItWorks: DAYS simply subtracts start_date from end_date using their underlying serial numbers. Because dates are stored as integers, the difference is the exact number of days between them, including leap days.

howToSteps.name: Enter end_date first
howToSteps.text: Provide the later date as the first argument.

howToSteps.name: Enter start_date second
howToSteps.text: Provide the earlier date as the second argument.

howToSteps.name: Read the day count
howToSteps.text: The result is end_date minus start_date.

limitations: Available only in Excel 2013 and later; in older versions use end_date - start_date directly.
The argument order is (end_date, start_date), the reverse of what many expect.
Text date strings must be parsed by Excel, otherwise you get #VALUE!.

commonErrors.cause: The arguments were supplied in the wrong order (start before end).
commonErrors.fix: Put the later date first: DAYS(end_date, start_date).

commonErrors.cause: One or both arguments are text Excel cannot interpret as a date.
commonErrors.fix: Use real date serials or DATE(...) so the values are numeric.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DAYS exists in Google Sheets with identical syntax and the same (end_date, start_date) argument order.

faq.question: Why is end_date the first argument?
faq.answer: DAYS(end_date, start_date) mirrors the subtraction end minus start; the order is easy to confuse with DATEDIF.

faq.question: What is the difference from DATEDIF?
faq.answer: DAYS returns total days; DATEDIF can return years, months, or day remainders.

faq.question: Does DAYS account for leap years?
faq.answer: Yes, because it works on serial numbers; Feb 29 simply exists as a day.
